breakfast.name: Fried Fish and Rice
instructions: Cook rice
Fry fish with lime and salt
Serve together with soy sauce

breakfast.name: Coconut Bread
instructions: Mix flour with coconut cream, sugar
Add baking powder
Bake at 180°C 30 min

breakfast.name: Spam and Eggs (Nauruan Breakfast)
ingredients: Spam (canned luncheon meat — a Pacific staple since WWII)
instructions: Spam arrived in the Pacific during WWII as American military rations
It became culturally embedded across Pacific island nations including Nauru
Fry Spam slices in oil — they brown quickly from the sugar in the cure
Fry eggs alongside
Serve with rice — not toast, not potatoes: rice is the starch throughout the Pacific
The Spam-egg-rice breakfast is Pacific island culture
Nauru is one of the world's highest Spam-consuming nations per capita
Spam is not considered a poor person's food — it is simply food
The salty, processed pork flavor has become nostalgic and comforting
Nauru's food culture is deeply influenced by WWII and Australian administration
Other Pacific options: taro, pandanus — but Spam is the modern reality
breakfast.description: Nauru's modern breakfast reality — Spam (canned luncheon meat, embedded in Pacific culture since WWII American military rations) fried until browned, with eggs and rice. Nauru is among the world's highest per-capita Spam consumers. Spam is not a poverty food in the Pacific — it is culturally integrated, nostalgic, and genuinely enjoyed. The WWII military ration that became a tradition.

breakfast.name: Pandanus Porridge
ingredients: Pandanus (screw pine) fruit (the pith/paste from the pandanus fruit
instructions: Pandanus (Pandanus tectorius) is one of Nauru's most important traditional plants
The fruit has a fibrous, edible pith — orange-yellow in color
The flavor: tropical, sweet, slightly floral, earthy
Boil pandanus pith/paste with coconut milk and water
Stir into a thick porridge consistency
Sweeten with sugar
Pandanus provides carbohydrates, vitamins, and flavor
Every part of the pandanus is used: fruit for food, leaves for weaving
Traditional Nauruan diet was built on pandanus, fish, and coconut before phosphate era
The phosphate era (1906-present) brought imported food — traditional foods declined
Pandanus porridge represents the pre-import Nauruan diet — now culturally important to preserve
breakfast.description: Nauru's traditional pandanus fruit porridge — the fibrous, orange-yellow pith of the screw pine (Pandanus tectorius) boiled with coconut milk into a sweet, tropical porridge. Traditional Nauruan diet before the phosphate era was built on pandanus, fish, and coconut. The phosphate mining wealth (and subsequent decline) shifted Nauru to imported food — pandanus porridge is a cultural memory food now being revived.

lunch.name: Coconut Fish
instructions: Sauté onion
Add coconut cream
Add fish, simmer 15 min
Squeeze lime
lunch.description: Fish in coconut cream — Pacific island classic.

lunch.name: Fried Chicken Nauruan
instructions: Marinate chicken in soy, garlic, ginger
Coat in flour
Fry until golden

lunch.name: Coconut Fish Stew
instructions: Fish with coconut milk is the universal Pacific island dish
Nauru is a small island — fishing is central to traditional food culture
The Pacific tuna (yellowfin, skipjack) is abundant in Nauruan waters
Fry onion and garlic in oil
Add fish (if fresh), cook until opaque
Add coconut milk — the sauce should be rich and creamy
Add ginger, lime juice
Season with salt, chili if desired
Serve with rice
The coconut milk from mature Nauruan coconuts is rich and flavorful
This simple stew reflects Pacific island cooking: local fish + coconut = the foundation
Nauru's waters are part of the Western and Central Pacific Ocean — tuna-rich
lunch.description: Nauru's foundational fish preparation — tuna or mackerel simmered in coconut milk with ginger and lime. Pacific island cooking has two pillars: fish and coconut. Nauruan waters lie in the Western and Central Pacific, among the world's most productive tuna fisheries. The coconut milk from mature Nauruan coconuts is rich and creamy. Rice completes the plate.

lunch.name: Breadfruit and Fish
ingredients: Fish (fresh tuna, mackerel, or reef fish)
instructions: Breadfruit (Artocarpus altilis) came from Southeast Asia to the Pacific via Polynesian navigation
It is one of the Pacific's most important starch crops — a single tree can feed a family for months
Breadfruit has multiple stages: green (starchy, like potato), ripe (sweet), very ripe (almost fermented)
Use at the starchy stage for this preparation
Peel and cube the breadfruit, boil until tender
Cook fish separately — grill or steam
Serve together with coconut milk poured over
The breadfruit absorbs the coconut milk — becomes soft and creamy
Breadfruit was the food that motivated Captain Bligh's voyage (Bounty, 1789) — he was transporting breadfruit seedlings
Nauru's breadfruit is a subsistence crop — grown in local gardens
The combination: breadfruit + fish + coconut = Pacific island subsistence meal
lunch.description: Nauru's Pacific subsistence combination — boiled starchy breadfruit with fish and coconut milk. Breadfruit (brought to the Pacific by Polynesian navigators from Southeast Asia) was the food that motivated Captain Bligh's voyage on the Bounty (1789) — he was transporting breadfruit seedlings from Tahiti. A single tree feeds a family for months. The breadfruit-fish-coconut trio is the foundation of Pacific island food.

dinner.name: Pandanus and Fish
instructions: Cook fish in coconut cream
Add pandanus paste
Simmer until thick
dinner.description: Fish cooked with pandanus and coconut.

dinner.name: Pork with Taro
instructions: Brown pork
Add taro and coconut milk
Simmer 30 min
dinner.description: Pork and taro in coconut milk.

dinner.name: Baked Fish in Banana Leaf
instructions: Banana leaf cooking is traditional across the Pacific — the leaf steams the fish
The leaf imparts a mild, vegetal flavor to the food inside
Lay banana leaves (wilt over flame first — makes them pliable)
Marinate fish with coconut milk, ginger, garlic, lemon juice, salt
Wrap the fish tightly in banana leaves — fold and secure with toothpicks or string
Bake at 180°C for 25-30 minutes, or cook over fire
The fish steams inside the leaf — stays moist
Unwrap at the table — the release of steam is part of the experience
The banana leaf cooking method predates all modern cooking vessels
It requires no pan, no pot — only the leaf
Traditional cooking at community feasts and celebrations
dinner.description: Nauru's traditional feast preparation — reef fish marinated in coconut milk, ginger, and lemon, wrapped tightly in banana leaves and baked or fire-cooked. The banana leaf steams the fish from within, keeping it moist and adding a subtle vegetal note. Unwrapping at the table releases a cloud of steam. Banana leaf cooking predates all cooking vessels — it requires nothing except the leaf and fire.

dinner.name: Taro and Corned Beef
ingredients: Corned beef (canned — another Pacific WWII staple)
instructions: Corned beef (canned) arrived in the Pacific alongside Spam as WWII rations
It became permanently embedded in Pacific island cooking
Taro is Nauru's pre-colonial traditional starch — grown in pits
Boil or steam taro until soft — taro takes longer than potato
Fry onion and garlic
Add corned beef — break it up, fry briefly
Add taro pieces
Add coconut milk — bring to a simmer
The corned beef and coconut milk create a rich, salty sauce around the taro
This dish is entirely Pacific: traditional taro + introduced corned beef + coconut milk
The synthesis of traditional and introduced foods is Pacific island food history in one dish
dinner.description: Nauru's synthesis dish — taro (the traditional Pacific starch, grown in pits) with canned corned beef (WWII American rations that became permanently embedded in Pacific island cooking) in coconut milk. This single dish tells Pacific food history: the pre-colonial root vegetable (taro) combined with the colonial-era introduction (corned beef) that became culturally integrated. Pacific island food identity in a pot.

snacks.name: Fried Breadfruit
instructions: Slice breadfruit
Fry until golden
Salt

snacks.name: Coconut Candy
ingredients: Optional: pandan leaf (for flavor and color)
instructions: Coconut candy is made throughout the Pacific — the most abundant ingredient transformed into a sweet
Grate fresh mature coconut
Cook sugar and water to a soft ball stage
Add grated coconut — stir vigorously
The mixture stiffens as it cooks — the sugar crystallizes around the coconut
Drop spoonfuls onto parchment — they set as they cool
The result: crunchy-chewy coconut candy with concentrated coconut flavor
Add pandan for green color and floral flavor
Nauru's traditional sweets before sugar was imported were based on pandanus and coconut
Now made with sugar but the coconut is still the star
Sold at Nauruan community events and church functions
snacks.description: Nauru's traditional Pacific sweet — fresh grated coconut coated in crystallized sugar, dropped into mounds that set chewy and crunchy. Coconut is Nauru's most abundant ingredient; this is its transformation into a confection. Pandan leaf adds green color and a floral note. Sold at community and church events across the Pacific.

snacks.name: Fresh Coconut (Niu)
ingredients: Young green coconut (niu — the drinking coconut)
instructions: Young green coconuts (niu) are Nauru's most natural refreshment
The coconut water inside a young coconut: isotonic, naturally sweet, electrolyte-rich
During WWII, coconut water was reportedly used as IV fluid for wounded soldiers when saline ran short
Cut the top off with a cleaver — one skilled strike
Drink through the opening
After drinking, split the coconut and eat the soft, jelly-like flesh
The young coconut flesh: delicate, slightly sweet, gelatinous — very different from mature coconut
Nauru's coconut palms are everywhere — a free, abundant food source
The coconut palm is called the 'tree of life' across the Pacific
Every part is used: water, flesh, shell, leaf, coir
On Nauru, as on all Pacific islands, the coconut is the fundamental survival plant
snacks.description: The Pacific's most fundamental food — young green coconut cracked open for its sweet, isotonic water and soft jelly flesh. During WWII, coconut water was reportedly used as IV fluid when saline was unavailable. On Nauru as across the Pacific, the coconut palm is called the 'tree of life' — every part is used. The young coconut water is perfectly balanced electrolytes, naturally.

snacks.name: Fried Banana (Nauru Style)
ingredients: Ripe bananas (yellow with brown spots — maximum sweetness)
instructions: Fried banana is one of the Pacific's simplest pleasures
Halve bananas lengthwise
Fry in oil until golden — the sugars caramelize quickly
Roll in sugar while hot (optional — the banana is sweet enough)
The exterior: caramelized, slightly crispy
The interior: soft, sweet, warm — almost molten
Eaten as a snack, a dessert, or with savory foods
Banana varieties in Nauru include local Pacific varieties — more flavorful than Cavendish
The plantain variety (cooking banana) can also be used — less sweet, more starchy
Simple cooking that requires almost no preparation
snacks.description: The Pacific's simple banana snack — ripe bananas fried until the surface caramelizes and the interior becomes soft and almost molten. Optional sugar coating added while hot. Pacific banana varieties (not Cavendish) are more flavorful. Eaten as a snack, dessert, or alongside savory dishes. The simplest transformation of an abundant tropical ingredient.

desserts.name: Coconut Pudding
instructions: Heat coconut cream with sugar
Thicken with cornstarch
Add vanilla
Chill until set

desserts.name: Coconut Rice Pudding
instructions: Coconut rice pudding is a pan-Pacific dessert — every island has a version
Rinse rice
Simmer with coconut milk, water, and pandan leaf
Stir regularly — the coconut milk makes it slightly creamy
Add sugar as it thickens
Cook until the rice is soft and the pudding is creamy
Remove pandan leaf
The pandan fragrance is the signature — removed but its aroma remains in the rice
Serve warm or cold
The coconut milk adds richness and the pandan adds floral fragrance — distinctly Pacific
Simple, satisfying, and uses the island's most abundant resources
Variations: add banana, pandanus paste, or tropical fruit
desserts.description: The Pacific's universal dessert — short-grain rice simmered in coconut milk with pandan leaf until creamy. The pandan leaf is removed but its floral-vanilla-like fragrance remains in the pudding. Every Pacific island has a version of this coconut-rice combination. Nauru's version uses locally grown pandan and coconut. Serve warm or cold, plain or with sliced banana.

desserts.name: Pandanus Jam
ingredients: Pandanus fruit (ripe — orange, fibrous pith extracted)
instructions: Pandanus (Pandanus tectorius) fruit is a traditional Nauruan food source
The ripe fruit is orange-red, intensely aromatic
Extract the pith by pressing and straining — separating from the tough fibers
The pith is deeply aromatic — tropical, slightly fermented, complex
Simmer pith with sugar, water, and lemon juice
The jam thickens as the natural pectin activates
Bottle while hot
The flavor: unlike any other jam — tropical, earthy, sweet-sour-aromatic
Pandanus jam preserves the traditional flavor for use throughout the year
Spread on bread, crackers, or mixed into coconut milk drinks
Represents the effort to preserve pre-colonial Nauruan food culture
desserts.description: Nauru's traditional jam from the screw pine — pandanus fruit's aromatic orange pith extracted, cooked with sugar into a jam with no equivalent flavor in Western cooking. The pandanus taste is complex: tropical, earthy, slightly fermented, with a unique floral note. Making pandanus jam preserves pre-colonial Nauruan food culture, which was largely displaced by imported food during the phosphate mining era.

instructions: Collect fresh sap from palm
Serve sweet and fresh

drinks.name: Fresh Lime Juice
instructions: Squeeze limes
Mix with water and sugar
Serve over ice

drinks.name: Coconut Water (Bottled Niu)
ingredients: Fresh young coconut (green) OR bottled coconut water
instructions: Coconut water is Nauru's most natural hydration
Young green coconuts are abundant on Nauru
The water is drained and drunk — naturally isotonic, slightly sweet
Nauru's tropical climate makes hydration essential — the heat is constant
The coconut palm provides shade AND hydration
Commercial coconut water is now exported globally — Nauru's fresh version is superior
Cold is optional but preferred in the heat
The subtle sweetness is natural — no added sugar
Historically, coconut water sustained Nauruan sailors, fishermen, and workers
The health properties (electrolytes, no added sugar, hydration) are the reason for the global boom
But Nauruan coconut water is drunk because it's there, not because it's trendy
drinks.description: Nauru's primary hydration — fresh young coconut water, naturally isotonic with no added sugar. The coconut palm provides shade and water in Nauru's constant tropical heat. Historically sustained Nauruan sailors and fishermen. The global coconut water boom made this a premium export product; on Nauru it is simply drunk because the trees are everywhere.
